messages:
customer_acme: Hey team — after we rotated the IdP signing cert at ~10:23 UTC, SSO logins to Redwood started failing. Users see 'SAMLResponse validation failed' and I see calls to your metadata URL returning 504 in our app logs. Can you triage?

sam_support: Sorry about that — we'll triage. Can you paste the metadata URL and a short repro (user + time)? Any error snippets from your logs would help.

customer_acme: Metadata: https://idp.acme-corp.com/saml/metadata.xml. Repro: try to SP-initiated login from our QA user. Our logs show this when Redwood tries to fetch metadata: `GET https://idp.acme-corp.com/saml/metadata.xml -> 504` but curl from our office returns 200.

irene_sre: Thanks. Two quick things to check: 1) is there a CDN in front of the IdP that may be returning 504 to our fetcher but 200 to your internal IPs? 2) can you run `openssl s_client` and paste the cert chain? Our metadata fetcher fails on TLS handshake in some cert-chain mismatch cases.

customer_acme: Running from our network: ```
$ curl -I https://idp.acme-corp.com/saml/metadata.xml
HTTP/2 200
server: nginx
content-type: application/xml
cf-cache-status: HIT
etag: "abc123"
```
But openssl shows only the leaf cert (no intermediate): ```
$ openssl s_client -connect idp.acme-corp.com:443 -servername idp.acme-corp.com 
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=idp.acme-corp.com
   i:/CN=Acme Corp Issuing CA (expired?)
---
no client certificate CA names sent
---
```
We asked webops to push the full chain but they said the CA rotated intermeidate earlier today.

lee_idp: From our side I can see MetadataFetcher logs around the same time: `ERROR MetadataFetcher - GET https://idp.acme-corp.com/saml/metadata.xml -> 504 (TLS handshake failed): java.security.cert.CertificateException: No subject alternative names matched` and also `CertPathValidatorException: validity check failed`. That looks like either missing SANs on the new cert or an incomplete chain. It also explains why curl from customer (with CDN/cache) returns 200 but our fetch from upstream IPs sees a different path.

sam_support: Ok actionable checklist: 
- please verify the IdP serves the full chain to public internet (openssl s_client -showcerts from an external host).
- confirm the leaf cert SANs include the metadata host (idp.acme-corp.com).
- if you have a metadata XML file, upload it to the Support Console / Admin -> Identity -> Upload metadata as a hotfix. That bypasses fetcher cache.

customer_acme: I uploaded the metadata XML to the Support Console (UI -> Identity -> Upload). Also ran from an external host: `openssl s_client -servername idp.acme-corp.com -connect idp.acme-corp.com:443` and it still showed only leaf cert, intermediate absent. Webops says their LB is misconfigured to omit the intermediate for certain edge POPs.

deploy-bot: Metadata refresh job scheduled: retry metadata fetch in 5m (job id: mf-2026-03-17-001).

irene_sre: While they fix LB, we can force a refresh and accept uploaded metadata. Sam, can you run the support tool to flush the metadata cache for entityId `https://app.redwood.com/saml/metadata/acme-corp` and apply the uploaded XML?

sam_support: Doing that now: `support-cli meta-refresh --entity "acme-corp" --force-upload --apply-uploaded` -> DONE. Travel time ~90s.

customer_acme: Confirming — users can login again, QA session succeeded at 10:46 UTC. Looks like upload + forced refresh worked. Thanks.

lee_idp: Root cause notes for tracking: IdP rotation omitted intermediate on some LB/edge POPs -> our fetcher sees incomplete chain -> TLS handshake fails -> metadata fetch returns 504 -> SSO fails. Fix: ensure LB pushes full chain, test from multiple external vantage points, and coordinate rotations with a short TTL on metadata cache or manual upload option.

sam_support: Agreed — next steps for you: 1) verify full chain on all edge POPs, 2) add a short cooldown and monitor during next rotation, 3) if possible publish metadata XML to your IdP endpoint with cache-control header that includes `max-age` and an explicit ETag. From our side: we documented a support playbook: - how to manually upload metadata, - how to force metadata fetch/flush, - checks to run (`openssl s_client`, `curl -v -H 'Host:'`). I'll DM the playbook link.

customer_acme: Appreciate the fast response. We'll follow up with webops to fix the LB chain and will schedule a coordinated rotation test with Redwood next week. :thumbsup:

sam_support: Closing this thread for now — reopen if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
